From: Bethany Cole <bethany@clearedge.com>
To: ops@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jan 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: High tail latency for model-v19 affecting user checkout (p95 spike)

Hi team,

We started seeing a sustained p95 tail-latency spike for the model-v19 route that powers our checkout autoprompts starting ~08:45 PST. Errors are not increasing, but user-perceived latency has risen from ~210ms to ~820ms at p95. This is impacting conversion on our largest merchant segment.

Attached is a short capture from our CI synthetic test and a link to a Grafana snapshot. Can you confirm whether this correlates to any recent variant rollouts or infra changes on your side? We need an ETA for mitigation or a temporary routing option to an older variant.

Thanks,
Bethany Cole
Head of Engineering Operations
ClearEdge Payments

Attachment(s): checkout-synth-20280109.csv (csv)

Bethany — thanks for the heads up and for the data. We're looking into model-v19 telemetry now. Quick summary of next steps: 

- Ben will pull the serving traces and KV/cache hit rates for the ClearEdge route.
- If this is a model regression, we'll prepare a controlled fallback to model-v18 for your traffic while we triage.
- I'll request a temporary SLO grace window while we remediate; want to keep you informed as we escalate.

Can you confirm the percentage of your traffic routed to model-v19 currently (approx)? That will help sizing the mitigation.

Subject: Re: High tail latency for model-v19 affecting user checkout (p95 spike)

Quick findings from initial triage: 

- Correlation: model-v19 rollout to ClearEdge pool occurred 2028-01-08 22:33 PST.
- Metric delta: p95 token latency for the route jumped from ~210ms to ~780ms between 08:42–08:49 on 2028-01-09. No significant change in CPU/GPU utilization on the host fleet.
- KV-cache hit-rate for that customer route dropped from 94% to 62% (prefix mismatch due to a tokenization change in the v19 tokenizer patch).
- No infra or kernel changes in prod at that time.

Mitigation options we can action immediately (ordered by how fast we can execute):
1) Traffic pinback: route ClearEdge traffic to model-v18 (stable) — 10–15m to implement and validate.
2) Soft rollback of tokenizer patch (risky without testing) — 60–90m and needs QA.
3) White-listing v19 cache warmup via replay of recent requests — 30–45m but requires coordination with ClearEdge for a synthetic replay window.

Recommendation: immediate pinback to model-v18 for safety, and initiate a tokenization rollback candidate in parallel. I can implement pinback as soon as I get approval from Markus to activate an SLO grace window for ClearEdge while we run the work.

Attachments: model-v19-kv-hitrate-20280109.csv (csv), p95-trend-model-v19-2028-01-09.png (png)

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Incident Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein <markus@redwood-inference.com>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood-inference.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood-inference.com>, Bethany Cole <bethany@clearedge.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2028 17:23:00 -0800
Subject: ACTION: Requesting temporary SLO grace window + traffic pinback for ClearEdge (model-v19)

Evelyn — I'm requesting authorization to activate a 72-hour SLO grace window and to pin ClearEdge traffic to model-v18 immediately. Rationale and plan below.

Why: model-v19 introduced a tokenizer patch that reduced KV cache hit rates on ClearEdge's prefix distribution, causing a sustained p95 tail-latency regression (~210ms -> ~780ms). The regression is customer-facing and materially impacts their checkout conversion.

Plan (timeline after approval):
- T+0–15m: Implement traffic pinback to model-v18 for the ClearEdge routed pool (Ben).
- T+15–45m: Validate end-to-end latency and conversion telemetry; if stable, mark the pinback as active.
- T+45–180m: Work on a controlled tokenizer rollback candidate and run QA in a canary on a small subset of traffic.
- T+12–72h: If rollback is safe, schedule a version bump; if not, work with ClearEdge on cache warmup replay plan.

Impact to SLOs: If approved, enable a 72-hour localized SLO grace window for ClearEdge only (we propose marking SLA exemptions for the route so this does not count against company-level availability metrics). This is a narrow, customer-scoped exception — not a platform-wide waiver.

Risk: Minimal platform-wide risk; this is a routing change and a temporary exception to avoid customer churn while we triage.

Request: Please confirm approval to (1) activate the 72-hour SLO grace window for ClearEdge and (2) allow immediate pinback to model-v18. If you approve, Ben will execute the pinback and I will notify ClearEdge and their CSM.

--
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
